title: Solver card
description: One solver's market listing for one network. Path: solvers/<network>/<name>.json

items.description: A Nostr relay URL the solver listens on.

nostr.description: Nostr transport config. `relays` is required; the object stays open to future nostr-specific settings.

transports.description: The v0 transport map. Nostr is the only supported protocol key.

id.description: Canonical asset identity: a CAIP-19-shaped id, "<chain-namespace>:<chain-reference>/<asset-namespace>:<asset-reference>". The chain namespace IS the corridor — bundled into the id rather than a separate base_corridor/quote_corridor field — so the id alone is a market side's whole leg identity: "arkade:bitcoin/slip44:0" (BTC on Arkade mainnet), "bolt11:bitcoin/slip44:0" (BTC over Lightning), "bitcoin:bitcoin/slip44:0" (BTC onchain), "arkade:bitcoin/asset:<68-hex>" (an Arkade-issued asset), "eip155:1/slip44:60" (ETH, the chain's own coin, on Ethereum mainnet), "eip155:1/erc20:0x…" (an ERC-20 on Ethereum mainnet). For arkade/bolt11/bitcoin the chain-reference is the Arkade network the side settles on (bitcoin, signet, mutinynet, regtest — the same vocabulary as the card's own path), and the slip44 reference it pairs with is fixed by that network, not open: 0 (Bitcoin) on 'bitcoin' (mainnet), 1 (Testnet, all coins) everywhere else — 'arkade:bitcoin/slip44:1' and 'arkade:mutinynet/slip44:0' are both malformed. For eip155 the chain-reference is the numeric EIP-155 chain id, and any chain id is well-formed — adding an EVM chain needs no schema edit, unlike the old per-chain corridor enum — with slip44 staying open there too, since it names whatever coin type that chain's own coin has. Lowercase throughout, not EIP-55 mixed case, so the identity is byte-comparable; the checksum belongs to display, not to a grouping key. The asset-namespace half also tells a taker WHICH SETTLEMENT path a corridor uses: "slip44" is a plain value transfer of a chain's native coin, "erc20" settles through that token's contract, "asset" is an Arkade-issued asset. An erc20 reference is the TOKEN's contract address, never a swap contract's — a taker resolves the latter from the corridor, not from this field.

decimals.description: Decimals of the atomic unit: atomic units per display unit = 10^decimals. Matches the asset registry metadata field.

type.description: The price feed response is JSON.

price_path.description: RFC 6901 JSON Pointer to the numeric feed value, e.g. /price or /bitcoin/usd. Empty string selects the whole JSON document.

amount.description: A canonical decimal-string amount of atomic units: unsigned, no leading zeros. "0" disables the side it bounds.

enabledAmount.description: An amount that is strictly positive: the side it bounds is enabled.

version.description: Card format version. 0 is every card written before EVM corridors existed. A card MUST declare 1 when any market side's asset id names a corridor introduced after 0 (today: eip155, i.e. any EVM chain); a consumer that understands only 0 MUST reject a version-1 card outright rather than interpret the markets it recognises and skip the rest. Bumping is about INTERPRETATION, not encoding: the canonical form and signature are unchanged, so a v0 verifier would still compute a matching digest — and would then be trusting a rail it cannot settle on.

name.description: Unique within the network directory; must equal the filename (without .json).

discovery_pubkey.description: BIP340 x-only public key, lowercase hex.

sig.description: BIP340 Schnorr signature by discovery_pubkey over sha256(canonical_json).

transports.description: Nostr relay URLs the solver listens on. Required — with discovery_pubkey and sig — when any market has a non-arkade corridor (the reducer enforces this cross-field rule): they are the rendezvous makers address request-for-quote messages to.

base_asset.description: The pair's base side. Its `id` carries the corridor (chain namespace) as well as the asset — see `#/definitions/asset`. When exactly one side's id names the arkade corridor it must be this side (the reducer enforces this), so equivalent corridor markets group under one canonical key.

quote_asset.description: The pair's quote side. Its `id` carries the corridor (chain namespace) as well as the asset — see `#/definitions/asset`.

price_feed.description: Required when the sides carry different assets; must be absent (with the other feed fields) on a same-asset market, whose price is identically 1 — fee_bps and fee_flat are the whole price and executable terms arrive in the solver's RFQ quote. The reducer enforces this cross-field rule.

price_decimals.description: The feed value divided by 10^price_decimals is the price in quote-atomic-units per base-atomic-unit.

fee_flat.description: The part of the price that does not scale with size, in quote-asset atomic units. OPTIONAL; absent means none. Quote-asset in both directions, matching min_quote_amount/max_quote_amount, so a client converts it through the price when the maker receives base. Note that fee_bps alone is therefore not a ranking key: a market with a lower spread and a flat fee can be dearer at small sizes and cheaper at large ones.

min_base_amount.description: Lower trade-size bound for the base side, in base atomic units. An enabled side has 1 <= min <= max; when the side is disabled (max = "0") min MUST be "0".

max_base_amount.description: Upper trade-size bound for the base side, in base atomic units. "0" disables the side: the solver does not pay out base and makers cannot receive it.

min_quote_amount.description: Lower trade-size bound for the quote side, in quote atomic units. An enabled side has 1 <= min <= max; when the side is disabled (max = "0") min MUST be "0".

max_quote_amount.description: Upper trade-size bound for the quote side, in quote atomic units. "0" disables the side: the solver does not pay out quote and makers cannot receive it.
